members: United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland

steps.intent: Our objective is to renew the 1718 Panel of Experts mandate for one year so that independent, fact-based monitoring of DPRK sanctions implementation, including evasion and arms transfers, can continue; the text is a clean technical rollover that preserves the resolution 2664 humanitarian carve-out. The hardest point is Russia, whose cooperation with the DPRK has been documented by the Panel and which may veto any renewal, leaving no realistic path to a zero-veto outcome if we insist on a full mandate. China may abstain, and we can likely secure nine votes, but securing Russian acquiescence would require concessions that would weaken the Panel’s independence.

China.change: Add: 'Reaffirming that the sanctions measures imposed by the Security Council should not have adverse humanitarian consequences for the civilian population of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea and should be implemented in accordance with international law, including the humanitarian carve-outs in resolution 2664 (2022);'

Replace with: 'Underscores that the Panel shall strictly adhere to its mandate and carry out credible, fact-based, independent assessments, analysis and recommendations in an objective and impartial manner; shall base its findings on verified information and give due consideration to information and comments provided by concerned Member States, including the country concerned; and shall respect the sovereignty, territorial integrity and political independence of all States and refrain from interference in their internal affairs;'

Add: 'Requests the Panel to include in its midterm and final reports an assessment of the humanitarian impact of the sanctions measures and recommendations to mitigate unintended humanitarian consequences, and to consult with all concerned Member States in the course of its work;'

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the draft as presented. Renewing the Panel's mandate is a technical measure that strengthens the credibility and effectiveness of the Council's sanctions regime, while resolution 2664 (2022) preserves humanitarian exemptions. We encourage the Council to maintain unity and to keep the door open to dialogue and a peaceful political settlement on the Korean Peninsula.
messages.China: China supports in principle a technical rollover of the Panel’s mandate, but the current text does not reflect our long-standing concerns. We ask the penholder to incorporate language ensuring that sanctions do not harm the humanitarian situation and that the Panel strictly adheres to its mandate, uses verified information and respects the views of concerned States. If these amendments are reflected, China can support the draft; otherwise we would have to abstain.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador supports the renewal of the Panel of Experts' mandate as set out in the draft and values the continued incorporation of resolution 2664 (2022). We consider credible, independent reporting essential to the implementation of the relevant sanctions measures and see no obstacles to the text as currently drafted. We look forward to joining consensus in favour.
messages.France: France supports the draft as presented. The extension of the Panel of Experts’ mandate is essential to preserve credible, independent monitoring of DPRK sanctions implementation and to uphold the Council’s unanimous resolutions. We urge all members to support a clean and timely renewal.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the renewal of the Panel of Experts mandate as drafted. We value credible, fact-based and independent reporting and the full implementation of existing measures. We have no amendments at this stage and encourage the Council to maintain unity on non-proliferation.
messages.Japan: Japan fully supports the renewal of the Panel of Experts’ mandate until 30 April 2025 as drafted. The Panel’s independent reporting remains essential in the face of the DPRK’s repeated ballistic missile launches, nuclear threats, and illicit arms transfers. Japan urges all Council members to support the text without weakening or delay.
messages.Malta: Malta supports the renewal of the Panel of Experts' mandate as drafted. Credible, independent monitoring and reporting are essential for the effective implementation of the Council’s DPRK-related resolutions. We encourage the Council to maintain unity and adopt the text without delay.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique supports the renewal of the Panel of Experts' mandate as set out in the current text. We value the Panel's credible, fact-based and independent work and call on all States to cooperate fully with the Committee and the Panel. We also stress the importance of applying the humanitarian exemptions under resolution 2664 (2022) and of pursuing peaceful dialogue on the Korean Peninsula.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea fully supports the one-year extension of the Panel of Experts mandate as drafted. The Panel's independent monitoring is essential to uphold the Council's sanctions regime and respond to the DPRK's continued violations. We urge all members to support the text without changes so that the Council can send a unified message.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot support the mechanical rollover of the Panel's mandate in its current form. The Panel's work has become politicized and unbalanced, and the Council should not endorse its findings and recommendations without a fundamental review. We insist on explicit humanitarian safeguards and strict impartiality; unless these red lines are reflected, we will not support the draft.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the renewal of the Panel of Experts mandate as drafted. Credible, fact-based monitoring remains essential to the implementation of the Council’s non-proliferation measures. We encourage continued impartial reporting and full cooperation by all Member States.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia fully supports the renewal of the Panel of Experts mandate until 30 April 2025. The Panel's independent, fact-based work is essential for the implementation of the sanctions regime and for addressing the DPRK's WMD and missile programmes. We have no changes to request and encourage all Council members to support the text as drafted.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland supports the renewal of the Panel of Experts’ mandate until 30 April 2025 and welcomes that the text preserves the resolution 2664 (2022) humanitarian carve-out. We value the Panel’s independent, fact-based reporting and encourage the Council to maintain consensus on this technical renewal. We have no changes to request at this stage.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom fully supports the renewal of the Panel of Experts' mandate as drafted. We urge all Council members to support a clean, timely extension so the Panel can continue its vital, independent monitoring of DPRK sanctions, including arms transfers and prohibited weapons programmes. We see no need for changes to the current text.

replies.China: rejected: amendments would constrain the Panel's independent mandate and create unnecessary reporting requirements; the existing reference to resolution 2664 already addresses humanitarian concerns
replies.Russian Federation: rejected: red lines would effectively prevent renewal and undermine the Panel's mandate

steps.summary: The penholder retained the clean one-year renewal, rejecting amendments that would weaken or delay the Panel's independent mandate. China is expected to abstain over rejected amendments, while Russia is expected to cast a veto, yielding 13-1-1.

messages.Algeria: Algeria supports the renewal of the Panel of Experts' mandate as set out in the current text. We believe the mandate's emphasis on credible, fact-based and impartial reporting, together with the humanitarian safeguards in resolution 2664 (2022), provides the appropriate basis. We therefore have no changes to request and will support the draft.
messages.China: China supports the proper and mandate-bound work of the Panel and has previously joined technical rollovers, but the current text still does not reflect our reasonable concerns on humanitarian impact, impartiality and respect for sovereignty. We reiterate our proposed amendments, in particular the humanitarian reaffirmation, the revised OP4, and the reporting requirement on humanitarian impact and consultation with concerned Member States. If these concerns remain unaddressed, China will abstain on the draft.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador supports the renewal of the Panel of Experts’ mandate as drafted. We value the Panel’s independent, fact-based work in supporting the implementation of the relevant Security Council measures. We encourage all Member States to cooperate fully with the Committee and the Panel, and we believe the text should be put to the vote without further changes.
messages.France: France fully supports the renewal of the Panel of Experts mandate as drafted. The Panel's work remains essential to the implementation of Security Council resolutions, and this text should be adopted without delay. We call on all Council members to support it and to reject any attempts to weaken the sanctions architecture.
messages.Guyana: Guyana supports the renewal of the Panel of Experts’ mandate until 30 April 2025 and believes the current text provides a sound basis for continued credible, fact-based monitoring. We underscore the importance of full cooperation by all States with the 1718 Committee and the Panel. Guyana is prepared to support the draft as it stands.
messages.Japan: Japan fully supports the current draft and welcomes the penholder’s balanced text renewing the Panel of Experts mandate until 30 April 2025. Given the DPRK’s continuing nuclear and missile activities, the Panel’s independent reporting and expertise remain essential to implementation of the sanctions regime. We urge all Council members to maintain unity and adopt the text without changes.
messages.Malta: Malta supports the extension of the Panel of Experts’ mandate and considers the current text balanced, fact-based, and consistent with previous Council resolutions. We particularly welcome the emphasis on credible, independent reporting and urge all States to cooperate fully with the Committee and the Panel. Malta has no changes to request and stands ready to support the draft as it is.
messages.Mozambique: The delegation of Mozambique supports the renewal of the Panel of Experts' mandate as contained in the current text. We welcome the penholder's inclusive consultations and have no changes to request at this stage. Mozambique remains committed to the full implementation of relevant Security Council resolutions and to credible, objective reporting by the Panel.
messages.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea fully supports the renewal of the Panel of Experts mandate as reflected in revision 1, and we thank the penholder for a balanced text. We urge all Council members to join consensus so that this Council can send a unified message that the DPRK’s unlawful WMD and missile programmes and illicit arms transfers will not be tolerated. The Panel’s independent monitoring remains essential to the effective implementation of the relevant resolutions, and we support the text as it stands.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot support the current draft, which simply extends the Panel for another year while ignoring the fundamental problems of politicization, double standards and humanitarian harm. Our red lines have been rejected, but they remain necessary conditions for any constructive consideration of this mandate. In the absence of such changes, we will vote against the draft.
messages.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supports the renewal of the Panel of Experts mandate as set out in the current draft. We value the Panel’s independent, fact-based reporting and the Council’s continued oversight of DPRK sanctions implementation. We have no changes to request and encourage the Council to adopt the text without delay.
messages.Slovenia: Slovenia supports the extension of the Panel of Experts' mandate through 30 April 2025 and welcomes the technical, fact-based focus of the draft. We believe credible and independent reporting remains essential to the full implementation of relevant Security Council resolutions. Slovenia is ready to vote in favour of the text as currently drafted.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland supports the renewal of the Panel of Experts' mandate as set out in the current draft. The Panel's credible, fact-based reporting remains essential for the implementation of the sanctions regime, and we welcome that the mandate continues to reflect resolution 2664 (2022) and its humanitarian carve-out. We therefore encourage all Council members to support the text as it stands.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom fully supports the renewal of the Panel of Experts' mandate and the current text. We see no need for changes: the Panel's independent, fact-based reporting remains essential to implementing the DPRK sanctions regime, including against evolving evasion and arms-transfer networks. We urge all Council members to support the draft and oppose any attempts to weaken or delay it.

steps.summary: The draft retains the one-year renewal of the Panel of Experts until 30 April 2025 and rejects amendments that would weaken its independence or cut the mandate short. It is expected to receive 13 votes in favour, with China abstaining and Russia voting against, resulting in a Russian veto.

reasons.Algeria: Algeria supported the renewal in the last negotiation round and has no objections to the unchanged text. As an elected member committed to non-proliferation and objective UN monitoring, it would vote in favour without needing to explain its vote beforehand.
reasons.China: China abstained because its proposed safeguards on the Panel’s mandate and humanitarian impact were rejected. This matches China’s stated concerns while avoiding a veto.
reasons.Ecuador: Ecuador consistently supports the DPRK sanctions monitoring mandate and voted for the prior renewal in resolution 2680 (2023). A routine technical extension of the Panel of Experts therefore warrants a vote in favour without the need for a pre-vote explanation.
reasons.France: France consistently supports extending the Panel of Experts’ mandate and strengthening implementation of DPRK-related sanctions. The draft aligns with France’s non-proliferation and regional-security priorities, so France votes Y.
reasons.Guyana: Guyana had signalled support for extending the Panel's mandate and generally favours multilateral non-proliferation measures and rule-based implementation of Council sanctions. A favourable vote is consistent with that position and with its concern for objective expert monitoring.
reasons.Japan: Japan firmly supports extending the Panel of Experts’ mandate to monitor DPRK sanctions implementation and will vote in favour. Consistent with its practice of explaining its vote after the vote, and its presiding role at this meeting, Japan does not take the floor before the vote.
reasons.Malta: Malta supports the mandate of the Panel of Experts as essential to credible monitoring of DPRK sanctions and consistent with its previous vote in favour of resolution 2680 (2023). It would therefore vote in favour of the draft extension.
reasons.Mozambique: Mozambique supported the previous mandate renewal and the current text in negotiations; extending the Panel is consistent with its support for multilateral non-proliferation and sanctions monitoring. No statement is needed for this routine renewal.
reasons.Republic of Korea: The Republic of Korea has consistently supported extending the Panel of Experts and condemning DPRK violations; as an elected member with a direct security stake, it would vote in favour and explain that vote before the vote.
reasons.Russian Federation: Russia had flagged the renewal as unacceptable without humanitarian safeguards and a review of the Panel, and its red lines were rejected; consistent with its policy against sanctions pressure, it votes no, ensuring a veto.
reasons.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone supported the draft in the last negotiation round and has a consistent interest in non-proliferation, strengthened sanctions monitoring, and the authority of the Security Council. The extension of the Panel of Experts is consistent with those priorities.
reasons.Slovenia: Slovenia has already signaled support and, as an EU member, backs the Panel of Experts mandate as a credible monitoring tool for DPRK sanctions. There is no indication it would take the floor before the vote.
reasons.Switzerland: Switzerland consistently supports renewing the Panel of Experts mandate and voted in favour of resolution 2680 (2023). The current draft retains the humanitarian carve-out and merits Swiss support.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK consistently supports renewing the DPRK Panel of Experts mandate as part of its non-proliferation and sanctions policy, and would vote yes. It would likely explain support before the vote, emphasizing accountability, DPRK violations, and cooperation with the Panel.
reasons.United States of America: The United States is the penholder and has consistently supported extending the Panel of Experts mandate. It would vote in favour and explain its support before the vote, emphasizing DPRK proliferation threats and the need for Council unity.

before.France: Mr. President, France will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The Panel of Experts is essential to the credible and impartial implementation of the Council’s sanctions, and its mandate must be renewed so that the Council can continue to monitor the DPRK’s unlawful nuclear and ballistic missile programmes, including the reports of arms transfers and military cooperation that undermine the non-proliferation regime. France condemns the DPRK’s continued violations and calls on all Council members to support this technical but necessary extension.
before.Guyana: Thank you, Mr. President. Guyana will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The continued nuclear and ballistic missile-related activities of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea, including its destabilizing launches, remain a serious threat to international peace and security and to the global non-proliferation architecture. The Panel of Experts provides the Council with essential independent, fact-based analysis and recommendations for the full and effective implementation of existing sanctions. We therefore support the renewal of its mandate and call on all Member States to cooperate fully with the Committee and the Panel, in accordance with their obligations under relevant Security Council resolutions. At the same time, Guyana stresses that sanctions should be implemented in a manner consistent with international law and should avoid unintended humanitarian consequences. We remain committed to diplomacy, dialogue, and the peaceful resolution of tensions on the Korean Peninsula.
before.Republic of Korea: Mr. President, the Republic of Korea will vote in favour of the draft resolution. The Panel of Experts remains essential to independent, fact-based monitoring of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s continued violations of Security Council resolutions, including its unlawful nuclear and ballistic-missile programmes and prohibited arms transfers. In the face of persistent provocations, the Council must maintain a clear and united position that such actions have consequences. My delegation urges all Member States to cooperate fully with the Committee and the Panel, and calls on the DPRK to abandon its weapons of mass destruction and ballistic-missile programmes, comply with its international obligations, and return to dialogue. Thank you.
before.Russian Federation: Mr. President, the Russian Federation will vote against this draft resolution. We have repeatedly stated that the sanctions machinery concerning the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea has become increasingly divorced from the goal of a political settlement and has serious humanitarian consequences for ordinary civilians. The Panel of Experts has been turned into a politicized instrument of pressure, while the penholder has rejected our proposals to reaffirm the humanitarian safeguards under resolution 2664 (2022), to review the Panel’s functioning and impartiality, and to ensure that its work remains strictly within its mandate. We cannot support a further extension on these terms. The problems of the Korean Peninsula must be resolved through dialogue and a balanced approach, not through endless restrictive measures and monitoring mechanisms that lack objectivity and impartiality.
before.Sierra Leone: Sierra Leone votes in favour of this resolution. We support the extension of the Panel of Experts’ mandate and the continued, objective monitoring of the implementation of the relevant Security Council resolutions. The proliferation of nuclear, chemical and biological weapons and their means of delivery remains a serious threat to international peace and security, and credible, fact-based reporting is essential for the Council to discharge its responsibilities. Sierra Leone also stresses that sanctions implementation must remain consistent with applicable humanitarian safeguards, including resolution 2664 (2022).
before.Switzerland: Switzerland will vote in favour of this draft resolution. The Panel of Experts is indispensable for credible, fact-based and independent monitoring of the sanctions regime, and its renewal is essential for the integrity of the work of the 1718 Committee. We welcome that the mandate continues to implement the humanitarian provisions of resolution 2664 (2022), and we call on all Member States to cooperate fully with the Committee and the Panel. Switzerland remains deeply concerned by the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s continued unlawful nuclear and ballistic missile activities, and we support a unified and effective Council response that upholds international peace and security while ensuring that humanitarian assistance can reach those in need.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Thank you, Mr President. The United Kingdom strongly supports the renewal of the mandate of the Panel of Experts. The Panel’s credible, independent and fact-based reporting is essential to the implementation of this Council’s resolutions and to exposing sanctions evasion, including illicit ship-to-ship transfers, cyber-enabled financial theft, and prohibited arms transfers. We condemn the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s continued unlawful ballistic missile launches and its nuclear and weapons programmes. We are also deeply concerned by reports of arms transfers from the DPRK to Russia in violation of this Council’s resolutions. Renewing the Panel is a necessary and practical measure to uphold the sanctions regime and prevent further destabilization. The United Kingdom urges all Council members to vote in favour of this resolution and to cooperate fully with the Committee and the Panel. We also stress that the sanctions regime is not intended to harm the people of the DPRK, and that humanitarian exemptions remain in place under resolution 2664. The DPRK must cease its provocations, abandon its weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missile programmes, and return to dialogue. The United Kingdom will vote in favour.
before.United States of America: Thank you, Mr. President. The United States strongly supports the renewal of the mandate of the Panel of Experts for an additional year. The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea continues to advance its unlawful nuclear and ballistic missile programmes in flagrant violation of this Council’s resolutions, and the Panel’s independent, evidence-based reporting remains indispensable to the implementation of the sanctions regime established by this Council. This is a straightforward renewal of a mandate that the Council has repeatedly supported. We urge all members to vote in favour and to uphold the credibility and integrity of this Council’s decisions.

after.Algeria: Mr. President, Algeria voted in favour of the draft resolution because we attach importance to the non-proliferation regime and to the full and effective implementation of the Security Council’s relevant resolutions. The Panel of Experts is a technical monitoring mechanism whose work should remain fact-based, objective and impartial. We regret that the Council was unable to renew its mandate today. Algeria stresses that sanctions must be implemented in accordance with international law and with the humanitarian safeguards contained in resolution 2664 (2022), so that they do not aggravate the suffering of civilians. We call on the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea to return to compliance with its international obligations, to refrain from destabilising actions, and to engage in dialogue. We also urge all Council members to preserve unity and to pursue a peaceful, diplomatic and comprehensive settlement of the Korean Peninsula issue. Thank you.
after.China: Mr. President, China abstained on the draft resolution just now. I wish to explain China’s position. China has consistently supported the denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula, the maintenance of peace and stability there, and the settlement of the issue through political and diplomatic means. China supports the full, complete and accurate implementation of the Security Council’s DPRK-related resolutions and supports the 1718 Committee and the Panel of Experts in carrying out their work strictly in accordance with their mandates. At the same time, the Council’s sanctions measures should not have adverse humanitarian impacts on the civilian population in the DPRK. The work of the Panel of Experts must remain objective, impartial and fact-based, and its reports should be credible and rigorous. The current situation on the Peninsula is complex and sensitive. The Security Council should focus on promoting dialogue, de-escalation and a political settlement, rather than simply extending the monitoring mechanism without a comprehensive review in light of the new developments. China made constructive proposals during the consultations and hoped that the draft would accommodate the legitimate concerns of all parties. Regrettably, those concerns were not fully reflected. That is why China abstained. China is ready to work with all Council members to play a constructive role in the political settlement of the Korean Peninsula issue. Thank you.
after.Ecuador: Mr. President, Ecuador voted in favour of this draft resolution and regrets that the Council was unable to renew the mandate of the Panel of Experts. The Panel’s work is technical and essential: it provides independent, fact-based monitoring of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s nuclear and ballistic missile programmes and of the implementation of this Council’s sanctions. Ecuador remains concerned by the DPRK’s continued launches and prohibited activities, which undermine international peace and security and the non-proliferation regime. At the same time, we reaffirm that sanctions must be implemented in full respect of international law and the humanitarian safeguards contained in resolution 2664 (2022), so that ordinary civilians are not adversely affected. Ecuador calls on all Member States to cooperate fully with the 1718 Committee, and we urge the Council to preserve credible and objective monitoring and to pursue unity, dialogue and a peaceful political settlement of the Korean Peninsula issue. Thank you.
after.France:
Mr. President,

France voted in favour of this resolution and deeply regrets that it was not adopted. The renewal of the Panel of Experts’ mandate was a technical and necessary measure to ensure credible, independent monitoring of the Council’s sanctions. The Panel’s fact-based reports are indispensable for exposing the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s unlawful nuclear and ballistic missile programmes, its sanctions evasion, cyber-enabled financial theft and prohibited arms transfers.

We deeply regret the Russian veto. It is a grave blow to the authority of this Council and to the international non-proliferation architecture. It does not relieve the DPRK of any of its obligations, nor does it weaken France’s commitment to the full implementation of the 1718 regime, including the humanitarian safeguards under resolution 2664 (2022).

France calls on the DPRK to abandon its weapons of mass destruction and ballistic missile programmes, comply with its international obligations and return to dialogue. We also call on all States to implement the Council’s resolutions in full and to cooperate with the 1718 Committee. France will continue to work with its partners to uphold international peace and security and to prevent the DPRK from further developing its unlawful programmes. Thank you.
after.Japan:
Mr. President,

Japan voted in favour of the draft resolution before the Council, and we deeply regret that it was not adopted owing to the negative vote of a permanent member. The mandate of the Panel of Experts is not a technical formality; it is essential to the credible, independent and fact-based monitoring of the Council’s sanctions regime. The Panel’s reporting on the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s nuclear and ballistic missile programmes, on sanctions evasion, and on prohibited arms transfers is indispensable to the implementation of this Council’s own decisions.

Japan strongly condemns the DPRK’s continued unlawful nuclear and ballistic missile activities, including its destabilizing launches and its development of nuclear weapon delivery systems, in flagrant violation of numerous Security Council resolutions. We are also gravely concerned by reports of DPRK-Russia military cooperation and arms transfers, which would constitute a serious violation of those resolutions and undermine the non-proliferation regime. Such cooperation must stop.

The failure to renew the Panel’s mandate weakens the Council’s ability to monitor and respond to these threats, and it erodes the credibility of the sanctions regime that this Council has unanimously built over many years. The existing sanctions remain in force, and all Member States must continue to implement them fully. Japan calls on all Council members to cooperate with the 1718 Committee and to preserve the Council’s unity and resolve in the face of the DPRK’s ongoing violations.

Japan will continue to work with partners to uphold the non-proliferation architecture, to promote the complete, verifiable and irreversible denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula, and to ensure that the Council does not remain silent while the DPRK advances its unlawful weapons programmes. Thank you.
after.Malta:
Mr. President,

Malta voted in favour of the draft resolution and regrets that the Council was unable to adopt it. The Panel of Experts performs a technical, independent and evidence-based function that is essential to the implementation of this Council’s sanctions regime and to exposing violations and evasion. We thank the Panel for its work.

The Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s continued nuclear and ballistic missile activities, including prohibited arms transfers, undermine international peace and security and the global non-proliferation architecture. Malta calls on the DPRK to comply fully with its international obligations and to return to dialogue without preconditions.

We underline that sanctions must be implemented in line with international law and with the humanitarian safeguards provided by resolution 2664 (2022). We call on all Member States to cooperate fully with the Committee and the Panel and to implement all relevant resolutions. The Council must remain credible and effective in upholding the non-proliferation regime and in supporting a peaceful, diplomatic and negotiated solution on the Korean Peninsula.

Thank you.
after.Mozambique: Mr President, Mozambique voted in favour of the draft resolution and regrets that the Council was unable to renew the mandate of the Panel of Experts. We did so because credible, fact-based and independent monitoring remains essential to the implementation of the Council’s non-proliferation decisions and to the integrity of the sanctions regime. Mozambique reaffirms its support for the denuclearization of the Korean Peninsula and for the peaceful resolution of concerns through dialogue and diplomacy. We also stress that sanctions implementation must remain consistent with the humanitarian safeguards contained in resolution 2664 (2022), so that ordinary civilians are not adversely affected. We call on the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea to comply with its international obligations and return to dialogue, and we urge all Member States to continue to cooperate fully with the 1718 Committee. The Council must remain actively seized of this matter. Thank you.
after.Republic of Korea:
Mr. President,
My delegation takes the floor to express its deep regret that the Security Council has failed to adopt the draft resolution renewing the mandate of the Panel of Experts. Thirteen members voted in favour, reflecting the clear will of the Council to preserve credible, independent and fact-based monitoring of the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s unlawful weapons of mass destruction and ballistic-missile programmes. The exercise of a veto on this straightforward technical renewal is deeply disappointing and weakens the integrity of the Council’s sanctions regime.
The Panel of Experts is not an end in itself. It is a necessary tool for implementing the Council’s resolutions, exposing sanctions evasion and prohibited arms transfers, and ensuring that the DPRK faces consequences for its continued violations. The Republic of Korea regrets that this outcome sends the wrong signal at a time when the DPRK continues to advance its nuclear and missile capabilities, including through destabilizing launches and illicit military cooperation.
My delegation calls on the DPRK to cease all provocations, abandon its weapons of mass destruction and ballistic-missile programmes, comply fully with its international obligations and return to dialogue. We also urge all Member States to continue to implement the relevant Security Council resolutions in full and to cooperate with the 1718 Committee. The sanctions regime remains in force, and the Council must not allow today’s decision to erode its authority. The Republic of Korea will continue to work with Council members and the international community to uphold peace and security on the Korean Peninsula and beyond. Thank you.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

The Russian Federation has voted against the draft resolution submitted by the United States. We did so deliberately and with full awareness of the consequences. This is not a vote against non-proliferation. It is a vote against the mechanical, indefinite extension of a sanctions-monitoring mechanism that has long since ceased to serve the purposes for which it was created and has become a politicized instrument in the hands of a narrow group of States.

We have repeatedly warned that the sanctions machinery concerning the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea is divorced from the goal of a political settlement and is causing serious humanitarian harm to ordinary civilians. The Panel of Experts has increasingly been used to justify further pressure and to advance unsubstantiated accusations against sovereign States. Its work must be strictly within its mandate, credible and impartial, and the humanitarian safeguards under resolution 2664 (2022) must be fully respected. We submitted constructive proposals to the penholder on these issues, including on reviewing the Panel’s functioning and ensuring its impartiality. Those proposals were ignored.

We also categorically reject the unsubstantiated allegations voiced today about alleged arms transfers from the DPRK to Russia. Such claims are not supported by reliable evidence and are an attempt to distract from the failure of the sanctions policy.

The Russian Federation remains committed to non-proliferation and to a balanced political settlement on the Korean Peninsula. But the Council must change its approach. Automatic extensions and ever-growing pressure are not a strategy. We will continue to oppose attempts to use the Security Council to advance narrow geopolitical interests. Thank you.
after.Slovenia: Thank you, Mr. President. Slovenia voted in favour of the draft resolution and deeply regrets that the Council has not been able to renew the mandate of the Panel of Experts. The Panel provides independent, credible and fact-based reporting that is indispensable for the implementation of this Council’s sanctions regime and for ensuring that our decisions are not undermined by evasion. We remain gravely concerned by the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s continued nuclear and ballistic missile activities, in violation of relevant Security Council resolutions, as well as by reports of prohibited arms transfers. A functioning monitoring mechanism is not a technical luxury; it is a core component of the sanctions regime this Council has established. We regret that a veto has prevented the Council from maintaining that mechanism at a time when our collective credibility is at stake. Slovenia will continue to support the full implementation of the relevant resolutions, including the humanitarian safeguards under resolution 2664 (2022), and we call on the DPRK to comply with its international obligations and return to dialogue. We also call on all Member States to cooperate fully with the 1718 Committee and to uphold the integrity of Council decisions. Thank you.
after.Switzerland: Mr. President, Switzerland regrets that the Security Council was unable to renew the mandate of the Panel of Experts. We voted in favour of the draft resolution because the Panel’s credible, independent and fact-based reporting is indispensable for the effective implementation of the 1718 sanctions regime and for the integrity of the Council’s decisions. Its work also helps ensure that sanctions are implemented in a manner consistent with the humanitarian safeguards affirmed in resolution 2664 (2022). The Council’s inability to renew this mandate should not weaken our collective resolve to address the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea’s unlawful nuclear and ballistic missile programmes. Switzerland calls on all Member States to continue to cooperate fully with the 1718 Committee, to comply with their obligations under relevant resolutions, and to support a peaceful and diplomatic resolution of the Korean Peninsula issue.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: Thank you, Mr President. The United Kingdom voted in favour of this resolution because the Panel of Experts is indispensable to the credibility and effective implementation of this Council’s DPRK sanctions regime. Its independent, fact-based reporting exposes sanctions evasion, illicit ship-to-ship transfers, cyber-enabled financial theft, and prohibited arms transfers. We deeply regret that the Council has once again been prevented from discharging its responsibilities by a Russian veto. This veto is especially cynical at a time of growing evidence that the DPRK has transferred ballistic missiles and munitions to Russia for use against Ukraine, in violation of this Council’s resolutions. Rather than addressing those violations, Russia has chosen to silence the very mechanism that documents them. We also regret China’s abstention. The United Kingdom remains resolute: the DPRK must abandon its unlawful nuclear and ballistic missile programmes, comply with its international obligations, and return to dialogue. Existing sanctions must be implemented fully and effectively, with the humanitarian safeguards under resolution 2664 (2022) upheld. We will continue to work with partners to uphold the non-proliferation regime and hold violators to account.
after.United States of America:
Thank you, Mr. President. The United States regrets that the Council has been unable to renew the mandate of the Panel of Experts. This was a straightforward, technical renewal. It was supported by thirteen members of this Council. It was blocked by a single permanent member: the Russian Federation. China abstained.

The Panel of Experts has provided this Council with credible, fact-based, independent reporting for years. Its work is not a matter of politics; it is a matter of implementing the binding decisions this Council has adopted. Today’s veto does not change the obligations of all Member States under those resolutions. It does not change the fact that the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea continues to advance its unlawful nuclear and ballistic missile programmes. It does not change the fact that this Council has prohibited the transfer of weapons and related material to and from the DPRK. And it does not change the danger posed by growing DPRK-Russia military cooperation, including reported transfers of munitions and ballistic missiles used against Ukraine.

We regret that Russia has chosen to undermine the Council’s ability to monitor sanctions implementation, including at a time when its own actions raise grave questions about its compliance with this Council’s resolutions. We also regret China’s abstention. The Council should be united in insisting that the DPRK comply with its obligations.

Let me be clear: the United States will not abandon these issues. We remain committed to the full implementation of the DPRK sanctions regime, to the humanitarian safeguards in resolution 2664 (2022), and to a diplomatic path that advances peace and security on the Korean Peninsula. We will continue to work with partners to ensure that violations are documented and that accountability is not extinguished by a single veto. We call on the DPRK to cease its unlawful provocations, return to dialogue, and choose the path of denuclearization and the well-being of its people. Thank you.
